Basford filled first position in both the 100yds. and 220yds. handicaps; Hayman was second in the Shot Putt and second in the 100yds.; whilst Penny's successes were first in the "half" and third in the mile. A popular win was that of Charlie Cook, who ran away with the Veteran's 100yds. handicap off 15yds.
A pack of cards appeared from someone's capacious pockets and we were amused (and paid for our amusement!) at C. Cook, Esq. calling “Twos” on Ace, King, Queen, Jack!

Hare were on the spot, as usual, and "Wee" Charlie Cook—who annually does a "smash and grab" raid right under the eyes of the City of London Police.
Jackman proved the winner, with that fine old-stager, Charlie Cook, second; and another one-time stalwart in Dicky Best, third. The 440 Yards was won in fine style by F.
Baumann, off scratch, second; and Dicky Best, third. Charlie Cook was also in the final, but did not display his customary "dash." For excitement the 880 yards handicap wanted some beating.
Who will promote a Veteran's Race for Charlie Cook to win in his eightieth year?

Our sympathies are extended to our old and esteemed Charlie Cook upon the loss of his wife. To Stan Blundon, whose father was killed in a dockside accident, and to Frank Thomson, our late President, upon the loss of his wife after a long and tedious illness.
Charlie Cook. Still running! and has run in Veteran's sprint handicaps, and thereby been in the limelight in what few sporting columns we get in the press nowadays.
Charlie Cook had his home demolished by a flying-bomb and sustained minor injuries necessitating a short stay in hospital. He recuperated at Woking where he saw Wally Bayliss a good deal.

Both schools wish to convey their thanks to those who so generously turned up to help—Tom Carter, Frank Thomson, Harry Shields, Charlie Cook, Bill Webb, and especially Alf Taylor who, being on night work, gave up his sleep to attend.
Charlie Cook is now back in the S.W.11 district again after being bombed out. The bomb had a bad effect on his hearing and we all sympathise with him.
Tooting Track is open for training every Wednesday evening at 7 p.m. to 9 p.m. Bob Jessop and Charlie Cook will be pleased to meet members at Tooting Track on Sunday mornings.
Dennis Rodaway was recently seen round the S.W.11 district by our old friend Charlie Cook. "Sailor" Johnson recently visited the Hall for a run when on leave.
Charlie Cook is recuperating and Will Inge has been ill. George Clay has been troubled by an old malady—an after-effect of being gassed in the 1914-18 war.
In reading his report we had a moment or two of thought for the passing of three of our club members: dear old Charlie Cook, Tom Sullivan and Rowland Rowbottom, which we all regret.
On the programme was the club hop, step and jump championship for a new club trophy, the “C. Cook” Cup, in memory of a very respected member, and this was won by P.
3 C.COOK

Our second picture features the man whose name is well known in the field event section----Charlie Cook. Each year the winner of our Triple Jump Championship is awarded the "Charlie Cook Memorial Cup", a trophy which remembers a unique Belgravian.

CHARLIE COOK also had his home demolished by a flying bomb and sustained minor injuries necessitating a short stay in hospital. JOHN BROWN lost his mother and a sister when their home was destroyed, and we extend to him our deepest sympathies.
Adams, C.
